note: Cross-layer formatting-locale cases (#23; PR #159 review, P3-2). Read by backend/tests/test_settings.py AND frontend/src/lib/locale-cases.test.ts, so a tag the backend stores that the browser's Intl formatter then throws on fails a test instead of reaching the Settings page. The backend asserts canonical_locale agrees with `canonical`; the frontend asserts Intl.getCanonicalLocales accepts every accepted input (producing the same canonical form) and throws on everything refused_everywhere. refused_by_policy is valid to Intl but deliberately refused by plamotrack — extension/private-use subtags would smuggle in a second hour-cycle or calendar — so the frontend only asserts those don't throw. `why` is for the reader; nothing asserts on it.

accepted.why: casing is canonicalised, not stored as typed
two distinct variants survive, in UTS 35's sorted canonical order — Intl sorts them, so unsorted storage would make one locale two settings
the other spelling of the same tag lands on the same canonical form
the 5-8 letter language window is shape-valid to Intl

refused_everywhere.why: four-letter language subtags are reserved in BCP 47; Intl throws
a repeated variant; Intl throws (the review's reproduction)

refused_by_policy.why: a -u-hc- extension is a second hour_cycle setting
a -u-ca- extension is a calendar setting this schema doesn't hold
private-use suffix carries meaning only its author knows
